source.speaker: Git documentation contributors
source.text:
merge.conflictStyle::
	Specify the style in which conflicted hunks are written out to
	working tree files upon merge.  The default is "merge", which
	shows a `<<<<<<<` conflict marker, changes made by one side,
	a `=======` marker, changes made by the other side, and then
	a `>>>>>>>` marker.  An alternate style, "diff3", adds a `|||||||`
	marker and the original text before the `=======` marker.  The
	"merge" style tends to produce smaller conflict regions than diff3,
	both because of the exclusion of the original text, and because
	when a subset of lines match on the two sides, they are just pulled
	out of the conflict region.  Another alternate style, "zdiff3", is
	similar to diff3 but removes matching lines on the two sides from
	the conflict region when those matching lines appear near either
	the beginning or end of a conflict region.

cebbee320b1a2dfd.question: {"as_of":"2025-03-14T16:19:41.000000+00:00","question":"Which Git configuration option chooses between basic and extended when grep.patternType is set to default?"}

answers.text: The Git configuration option that chooses between basic and extended when grep.patternType is set to default is grep.extendedRegexp.

evidence.speaker: Git documentation contributors
evidence.quote: value 'default' will use the `grep.extendedRegexp` option to choose

expected.question: Which Git configuration option chooses between basic and extended when grep.patternType is set to default?

historical_citations.quote:
Using a value of 'basic', 'extended',
	'fixed', or 'perl' will enable the `--basic-regexp`, `--extended-regexp`,
	`--fixed-strings`, or `--perl-regexp` option accordingly, while the
	value 'default' will use the `grep.extendedRegexp` option to choose
	between 'basic' and 'extended'.

source.speaker: Git documentation contributors
source.text:
grep.patternType::
	Set the default matching behavior. Using a value of 'basic', 'extended',
	'fixed', or 'perl' will enable the `--basic-regexp`, `--extended-regexp`,
	`--fixed-strings`, or `--perl-regexp` option accordingly, while the
	value 'default' will use the `grep.extendedRegexp` option to choose
	between 'basic' and 'extended'.
